title: Greedy Best-First in SF: Rush vs Real Routes ⚡
description: Watch Greedy Best-First sprint toward a goal using only a heuristic estimate. Then see exactly how it can miss the shortest path when the “closest-looking” route turns out to be a trap.
ig_caption:
Greedy Best-First Search vs A*: Pathfinding Comparison — Why Greedy Best-First rushes to the destination ⚡

In this SF Mission District map viz, each node’s priority is purely: f(n)=h(n). That means Greedy Best-First ignores the real cost so far (g), unlike A* (which balances g+h). ✅

What you’ll see in the animation:
• The algorithm constantly expands the node that “looks closest” to the target.
• It often works fast when the heuristic is aligned with the true path.
• It can fail spectacularly when local shortcuts lead to dead-ends or detours—classic greedy behavior.

Takeaway: A* is usually safer for optimal paths; Greedy Best-First is great for speed when you’re okay with “good-enough” routes.

Debate question: In your experience, should pathfinding optimize for fastest discovery (Greedy) or guaranteed optimality (A*)?
